clue.text: Builds on mouthful, formerly crumbled crust

parts.note: a sup is a small mouthful of drink

indicators.note: something crumbled has broken apart, so the word before it is broken up and its letters reset

parts.note: erst is an archaic word for formerly
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats a mouthful, and the old crust falls to crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To superstruct is to build something on top of a foundation, so it is a verb matching the phrase.

clue.text: We had vehicle lifting old cow

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting lets the letters run upward, so the pair is read from bottom to top

parts.note: we had contracts to we'd
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A group remembers a car that once lifted an elderly cow.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBDEW is an obsolete spelling of subdue, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission, an older sense of subdue in its archaic spelling.

clue.text: Lead player very precise over orchestra's introduction

parts.note: prim means stiffly correct and proper

parts.note: first letter of orchestra

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.

clue.text: Like shallow chatterbox, husband penned a dead letter clumsily

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in, so one piece is enclosed by the others
done clumsily means put together awkwardly, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A gossipy husband writes an awkward note that never gets delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: The H goes in among the eleven letters of 'a dead letter' and all twelve are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattle-headed describes an empty, giddy person who chatters without thought, as a rattle makes noise with little inside.

clue.text: Theologian's disciple have bothy during stay in Scotland?

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls inside it, so one piece sits within the other

a bothy is a Scottish hut, and a cot is a small cottage

explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a rough shelter for walkers in the Scottish hills; the question mark flags that 'stay' is being used in its Scots law sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotist is a follower of the medieval theologian John Duns Scotus.

clue.text: Announced like Bells on Sunday as broadcast

parts.note: church bells are tolled on a Sunday

explanation.surface: Something was proclaimed like church bells ringing out on the radio on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Bells on Sunday is also a long-running BBC radio programme of church bells, which suits 'broadcast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Told is a past tense meaning made known or related, the same as announced.

clue.text: Ten trees, on this, having to blend in, rising

definitions.text: Ten trees, on this, having to blend in, rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upward, so the letters run backwards
having means holding, so one group of letters keeps another inside it
on this means undergoing the very process the clue defines, being moved to new places, so the letters are relocated

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to melt into something is to blend with it

explanation.surface: Trees being transplanted must blend into their new site as they grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: trees put through resettlement have to blend into new ground, and the word 'this' points at the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Resettlement is moving things to a new place to establish them there, as when trees are transplanted.

clue.text: Abnormal droop? Beginning thereof observed in foot

indicators.note: something observed in a place is seen inside it, so the one letter goes within the other word

the first letter of droop, the word 'thereof' points back to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' tempts as a body part, but here it is a unit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Chordee is a medical condition where the penis curves downward, an abnormal bending.

clue.text: Sudden pain, last bit working most of way up, working up as before

indicators.note: moving most of the way up a down entry puts a letter back in near the top, just inside the first one
the last bit is the final letter, which is taken off its word to be used elsewhere

parts.note: a twinge is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: A sharp pain creeps up as before while someone is busy working.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of TWINGE climbs to just under the T, stopping one short of the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tew is an old and dialect verb meaning to work hard or toil, so tewing is the obsolete sense of labouring.

clue.text: Poet's passion, making mark in Scottish hillside

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word that follows it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' signals an old word used by Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Brame is a Spenserian word for intense longing or strong feeling.

clue.text: Terrible aches etc. about love, uncontrollable desire

love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

clue.text: Musical bar displaying Maori's home amid the waves?

clue.text: Source of fashion, No. 1 in spectacular bust

clue.text: Scottish sheep? Our lot will follow your lot mostly

clue.text: Dull old copper coin, penny

parts.note: the dam was an old Indian copper coin

clue.text: Annoyance when denied cha? Look pained possibly

clue.text: Soften mealie, lot in mixture

clue.text: Water round front of piston was leaking

clue.text: Confusion involving drizzle for member of colony?

clue.text: Liqueur Turkey bottled matures, knocked back

clue.text: Poet's taunt, very firm, about women

clue.text: What's healthy, interrupting work, not OK? It's after school
